name: Encompass
tagline: Tandem's early-1980s fault-tolerant distributed database system, the predecessor of NonStop SQL.
description: ENCOMPASS was Tandem Computers' distributed database management system for its fault-tolerant NonStop machines, documented in Tandem technical reports from 1981. It was a suite rather than a single engine: the ENSCRIBE record manager (key-sequenced, relative and entry-sequenced files with alternate keys), the TMF Transaction Monitoring Facility for atomic transactions with audit trails across nodes of an EXPAND network, the PATHWAY transaction-processing monitor, a data dictionary, and ENFORM, a relational query and report language over ENSCRIBE files. That stack ran many 1980s ATM, banking and stock-exchange systems. Tandem replaced the relational layer with NonStop SQL in 1987, but Enscribe, TMF and Pathway survive in today's HPE NonStop platform.
statusNote: Superseded by NonStop SQL (1987). Its components Enscribe, TMF and Pathway still ship on HPE NonStop; use HPE NonStop SQL for new work.

pricing.notes: Sold with Tandem NonStop systems; no longer offered.

scale.notes: Files could be partitioned across processors and EXPAND network nodes, with TMF coordinating distributed transactions.

strengths: Fault-tolerant, distributed transactions (TMF) years before most databases had them
Data partitioned across processors and network nodes, transparent to applications
Proven in 1980s banking, ATM and exchange workloads
Core pieces (Enscribe, TMF, Pathway) are still supported on HPE NonStop
weaknesses: Tied to Tandem/NonStop hardware and its proprietary toolchain
ENFORM was a query/report language, not full SQL; replaced by NonStop SQL
Historical documentation is mostly scanned manuals and technical reports
useCases: Understanding the lineage of HPE NonStop SQL
